body.def: Situation, Problem, Implication, Need-payoff questions in sequence. The proprietary research reported that in complex sales only explicit, buyer-stated needs predicted success.
body.mech: Implication questions are loss framing; need-payoff questions resemble change talk; the sequence is follow-up questioning by design.
body.app: Diagnose before prescribing. Note that its core mechanism inherits the loss-aversion dispute.

sources: Rackham (1988), SPIN Selling — Huthwaite proprietary research
open: The underlying dataset has never been independently audited.

label: Gap Selling

body.def: Map current state against desired state; the size of the gap is the deal.
body.mech: Practitioner framework restating SPIN's diagnostic sequence.
body.app: If the gap cannot be articulated, there is no deal yet.

sources: Keenan (2018), Gap Selling

label: The Challenger Sale

body.def: Teach, tailor, take control. Proprietary rep-profile research reported relationship-builders as weakest and challengers strongest in complex B2B.
body.mech: An agency-axis strategy: insight plus willingness to push back.
body.app: The curvilinearity finding is a direct problem for this: maximising agency signalling is predicted to reduce perceived warmth, which the framework treats as costless.

sources: Dixon & Adamson (2011), The Challenger Sale
open: Unreplicated outside the originating organisation.

label: The Trusted Advisor

body.def: Trust modelled as credibility plus reliability plus intimacy, divided by self-orientation.
body.mech: A communion-axis playbook. Not an empirical equation — a mnemonic.
body.app: Lowering self-orientation is the lever most under your control.

sources: Maister, Green & Galford (2000), The Trusted Advisor

label: The JOLT Effect

body.def: Analysis of a large proprietary corpus of recorded sales conversations concluding that stalled deals are driven by fear of a wrong decision rather than preference for the status quo, with fewer options and a clear recommendation as the remedy.
body.mech: Combines loss framing, blame-avoidance and closure need. Requires autonomy to be preserved or the close unravels later.
body.app: Do not add options to a stalled decision.

sources: Dixon & McKenna (2022), The JOLT Effect
open: Proprietary corpus, not independently auditable.

label: Never Split the Difference

body.def: Labeling, mirroring, calibrated questions and tactical empathy, derived from negotiation practice rather than controlled testing.
body.mech: Labeling borrows a solid mechanism (affect labeling); mirroring borrows a modest one (mimicry); calibrated questions resemble MI's open questions. The package has not been tested as a package.
body.app: Label before solving. The components have very different evidential backing and the book does not distinguish them.

sources: Voss & Raz (2016), Never Split the Difference

label: Art of Seduction archetypes

body.def: Nine seducer archetypes plus an anti-seducer, drawn from history and literature. Not empirical psychology and not presented as such by its author.
body.mech: Mapping the archetypes onto the social-evaluation axes is my synthesis, not a claim in the book or the literature. [synthesis]
body.app: Usable as a tactics library only when read through the validated nodes it connects to. Two specific empirical problems: high-agency archetypes are predicted to cost warmth, and intermittent-availability tactics are predicted to select for anxious attachment rather than build secure bonds.

sources: Greene (2001), The Art of Seduction
open: v1 gave this node fourteen links, most decorative. Cut to four defensible ones. A literary typology should not be one of the most connected nodes in a map of psychology.

label: Overcorrection in validity estimates

strength.label: solid
strength.replication: Published in Journal of Applied Psychology and broadly accepted as a methodological advance rather than a contested claim.
strength.magnitude: Applied to cognitive ability and job performance, the long-quoted .51 figure was revised to .31 for twentieth-century data; a meta-analysis restricted to twenty-first-century studies found a mean observed validity of .16 across 153 samples (N=40,740), rising to .22 after defensible corrections.
strength.boundaries: Concerns correction methodology, not whether the predictors work. All of these relationships remain positive and real; they are smaller than commonly taught.

body.def: A methodological correction affecting how every predictive validity figure in personnel and individual-differences research should be read. Standard meta-analytic practice applied range-restriction corrections 'across the board', including to concurrent studies where the correction is not warranted.
body.mech: Because current employees were not selected on the assessment being studied in concurrent designs, applying a restriction correction inflates the estimate. The inflation compounds with criterion-unreliability corrections.
body.app: Any confident effect size you encounter from pre-2022 selection research is probably inflated. This node exists to make that discount automatic rather than a thing you remember sometimes.

sources: Sackett, Zhang, Berry & Lievens (2022), Journal of Applied Psychology — 'Revisiting Meta-Analytic Estimates of Validity in Personnel Selection'
Sackett, Demeke, Bazian, Griebie, Priest & Kuncel (2023), Journal of Applied Psychology — 153 samples, N=40,740
open: How far the same overcorrection extends into personality, interview and assessment-centre literatures. Partially addressed, not settled.

label: Citation fabrication (this atlas's own failure)

strength.label: solid
strength.replication: Repeated searching across multiple phrasings failed to locate the cited work.
strength.magnitude: One fabricated citation was found in a sample of roughly eight nodes audited. That rate should not be extrapolated confidently from such a small sample, but it is not reassuring either.
strength.boundaries: Applies to every node still marked inherited in this map.

plain.what: A note recording that an earlier version of this atlas cited a paper that does not appear to exist.
plain.why: It is here because a map that grades everyone else has to be willing to grade itself.
plain.catch: Invented citations look exactly like real ones. That is why anything not yet checked is labelled unverified rather than quietly trusted.

body.def: A node recording a failure found in this document rather than in the literature. v1 contained at least one citation to a paper that does not appear to exist, written from pattern rather than from a source.
body.mech: Plausible-sounding citations are generated fluently and are undetectable to a reader who does not check. The failure is silent: nothing about the surrounding text looks different.
body.app: The practical rule this imposes: verification status is displayed on every node, inherited nodes show deliberately less detail, and no inherited citation should be quoted to anyone else until it has been checked.

sources: Cycle 0 audit, this document
open: How many more exist. Each cycle re-verifies the inherited nodes in its own domain.
